response_text:
Network for Good (now rebranded as **For Good** for its donor-advised fund arm) is widely used but has a recurring pattern of complaints around **fund disbursement delays, fees, and customer support**, alongside some workflow issues for nonprofits.[2][4][7]

Here are the main types of problems people report, plus context that helps explain them:

## 1. Delays in getting donations disbursed

- Nonprofits and users have reported **trouble getting large donations disbursed** or delays in receiving funds.[2]  
- Earlier commentary on Network for Good’s processing model notes that donations are often **batched and sent to nonprofits only once a month**, not in real time.[1]  
- Because of this, a donor may give on a certain date, but the nonprofit might not actually receive the funds for several weeks.[1]  
- This delay can also create **acknowledgment problems**: nonprofits that wait for the money to arrive before thanking donors end up looking unresponsive, even though Network for Good does send an *automated* receipt immediately.[1]

**What to do if this is your issue:**

- Log into your **Network for Good / Bonterra portal** to verify the donation is recorded.[9][10]  
- Confirm whether your organization is set up for **EFT (direct deposit)**; otherwise funds may be mailed by check on a monthly cycle.[1]  
- If a check is expected, confirm your **mailing address and charity profile** are correct in Guidestar/Candid, since Network for Good pulls data from there.[1]  
- If there is a specific missing or delayed large donation, you may need to open a ticket with Bonterra/Network for Good support with:
  - Donation date and amount  
  - Donor’s name and email (if known)  
  - Your organization’s EIN and account info  

## 2. Confusion about donor information and acknowledgments

- Network for Good (as a DAF/payment intermediary) issues an **automatic email receipt** labeled “Thank You for Your Support,” but this functions as a *transaction receipt*, not a personalized acknowledgment from the nonprofit.[1]  
- Some nonprofits assume that automated message is sufficient, so donors never receive a **proper thank-you or follow-up**, which harms relationships.[1]  
- Donors can choose whether to **share their contact information** with the nonprofit; if they opt out, the organization may only see limited details and cannot follow up directly.[1]

**Mitigations for nonprofits:**

- **Sign up for daily email notifications** of donations so you see gifts as they come in rather than waiting for a monthly payout.[1]  
- Build a workflow to **send your own thank-you within a week**, independent of when funds are deposited.[1]  
- When donor contact info is shared, **add them to your email/newsletter list** (with clear opt-out) and include them in standard stewardship and renewal cycles.[1]

## 3. Fees and cost concerns

- Network for Good charges **transaction processing fees, generally 3–5%**, plus any subscription fees for its fundraising and donor management platform.[4]  
- Some nonprofits describe the service as **“VERY expensive” with “extra fees” and not worth the cost** for what they receive.[7]  
- Donors or nonprofits may be surprised to see a sizable portion of each gift going to platform and processing fees if this is not communicated clearly.[4][7]

**What you can do:**

- Review your contract or fee schedule: processing fees, platform subscription, and any add-ons.  
- Decide whether to:
  - Absorb fees as an org cost,  
  - Ask donors if they are willing to cover processing fees, or  
  - Use Network for Good only for certain campaigns while using lower-fee methods elsewhere.  
- If cost is the primary concern, compare with alternatives (other CRMs or fundraising platforms) and factor in:
  - Subscription price  
  - Payment gateway fees  
  - Staff time saved or lost  

## 4. Customer support and responsiveness

- On reviews sites, some users report **“terrible customer service”**, stating that issues are **not resolved timely or properly**.[7]  
- These complaints often relate to:
  - Unresolved **payment or disbursement questions**  
  - Difficulty getting help when something in the donor data or reporting does not look right  
  - General frustration with responsiveness relative to the cost of the service[7]

Because these are anecdotal reviews, they should be weighed against the large user base and the company’s claims of strong results for many nonprofits, but they do show a pattern of dissatisfaction among a segment of users.[3][4][5][7]

**If you’re currently stuck:**

- Document the issue clearly (screenshots, dates, amounts, error messages).  
- Use any **dedicated support channels** provided in your contract or admin portal, and request a **case number** so you can follow up.  
- If you are not getting responses, escalate within your organization to the person who owns the vendor relationship so they can push on the account-management side.

## 5. Platform / workflow limitations (for nonprofits)

As a fundraising and donor management platform, Network for Good (now part of Bonterra) promises an **all-in-one solution** with donor database, campaigns, communications, and events.[4][5][6] Some common pain points users report with systems like this (including in reviews of Network for Good) include:

- Feeling **locked in** to a single system that doesn’t integrate smoothly with other tools.  
- Limitations in **reporting or customization** for more complex organizations.  
- Learning curve for staff and the need to re-train when the platform is updated or rebranded (e.g., acquisition by Bonterra and evolution into “For Good”).[4][5][8]

On the other hand, many smaller nonprofits do value the “all in one, simpler than enterprise CRMs” approach the company markets.[5][6]

---

If you tell me which side you’re on—  
- donor trying to track or get credit for a gift,  
- nonprofit trying to receive a specific donation,  
- or an organization evaluating whether to keep or leave Network for Good—  
I can walk you through concrete next steps tailored to your situation (including specific wording to use when contacting support or communicating with donors).
